title: Industries We Document
summary: Ten industries, one pattern. Each is built somewhere on a body that could not agree to it. For each we keep a standing reference — the single most useful public investigation or database in that field — alongside our own field notes.

resource.title: #BeCrueltyFree — Country-by-Country Cosmetics Testing Tracker
resource.body: The most comprehensive public tracker of which jurisdictions have banned cosmetics testing on animals, where loopholes still exist, and which bills are in motion. Updated continuously as policy changes. Essential reference work for anyone trying to verify a “cruelty-free” claim against the law that actually applies.
resource.label: Read at HSI

resource.publisher: The Sunday Times · 2020 · Boohoo Leicester investigation
resource.title: Inside Britain's Sweatshops: Boohoo, Leicester, and Sub-Minimum-Wage Garment Work
resource.body: The undercover reporting that documented Leicester garment factories paying workers under UK minimum wage to supply Boohoo. Triggered the Garment and Textiles Workers Trust review and remains the most consequential UK garment investigation of the last decade.
resource.label: Read at The Times

resource.publisher: The New York Times · 2023 · Hannah Dreier
resource.title: Alone and Exploited: Migrant Children in US Meatpacking
resource.body: Pulitzer-winning investigation documenting unaccompanied migrant children working in US slaughterhouses and food-processing plants, often through subcontracted cleaning agencies. Led to Department of Labor enforcement actions and a federal interagency taskforce.
resource.label: Read at NYT

also.title: Compassion in World Farming — research reports

resource.publisher: World Animal Protection · ongoing research programme
resource.title: Wildlife Tourism Investigations — Tracking the Travel Industry
resource.body: World Animal Protection's standing research library on wildlife used for entertainment. Tracking the Travel Industry scores named travel companies and booking platforms on the attractions they sell; Paradise Lost and Bred to Entertain document conditions on the ground in Bali and Thailand. The scoring methodology is published, so a claim about a specific operator can be traced back to what was actually observed.
resource.label: Read at WAP

resource.publisher: SOMO & India Committee of the Netherlands · multiple reports
resource.title: Captured by Cotton: The Sumangali Scheme in Tamil Nadu Garment Mills
resource.body: Years of documentation on the bonded-labour scheme targeting young women in South Indian spinning mills — multi-year contracts, lump-sum payments framed as dowry, confined accommodation. Names supplier factories and the major brands sourcing from them.
resource.label: Read at SOMO

resource.title: Revealed: More Than 90% of Rainforest Carbon Offsets by the Biggest Provider Are Worthless
resource.body: The investigation that broke open the voluntary carbon market. Analysed Verra's rainforest credit programme and found a substantial majority of credits did not represent real emissions reductions. The fallout reshaped corporate offset strategies worldwide.
resource.label: Read at The Guardian

resource.title: “This Is What We Die For”: Human Rights Abuses in the DRC Cobalt Trade
resource.body: The foundational report mapping artisanal cobalt mining in the Democratic Republic of Congo to global consumer-electronics supply chains. Documented child labour, fatal accidents, and severe health consequences, and named the brands sourcing from the affected trade.
resource.label: Read at Amnesty

resource.title: Green Claims Code — Investigations into ASOS, Boohoo, Asda and Unilever
resource.body: The CMA's enforcement portfolio against misleading environmental claims. The 2022 ASOS / Boohoo / Asda case forced commitments to substantiate or remove sustainability claims. The 2023 Unilever investigation extended the same scrutiny to FMCG.
resource.label: Read at GOV.UK

resource.publisher: Business & Human Rights Resource Centre · ongoing
resource.title: Allegations Tracker — Corporate Human Rights Abuses
resource.body: The single most useful open database in this space. Tracks alleged corporate human-rights abuses and each company's response — or refusal to respond. Searchable by company, country, industry, and issue. If a brand has been named in a major investigation, it is here.
resource.label: Read at BHRRC

resource.publisher: UK Advertising Standards Authority & CMA · 2021 sweep
resource.title: An Influencer's Guide — Disclosure Compliance Monitoring
resource.body: The 2021 monitoring sweep documented widespread non-disclosure of paid promotion across UK influencer Instagram and TikTok accounts. The ASA followed up with public rulings against named accounts, and the accompanying Influencer's Guide remains the clearest statement of what disclosure actually requires.
resource.label: Read at the ASA
